players.product: Silicon carbide (SiC) substrates: conductive, semi-insulating and P-type (6/8-inch volume, 12-inch launched); also optical-grade SiC for micro-nano optics

quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 results (annual report): revenue RMB 1,464,882,451.01, down 17.15% from RMB 1,768,140,956.17; net profit attributable to shareholders RMB -208,319,118.23 versus RMB 179,025,054.91 in 2024 (-216.36%); net profit excluding non-recurring items RMB -245,899,387.11. Quarterly revenue: Q1 RMB 407,961,034.96, Q2 RMB 385,844,167.99, Q3 RMB 318,200,911.07, Q4 RMB 352,876,336.99; Q4 net profit attributable RMB -209,439,019.13. The company said SiC substrate sales volume grew significantly (faster than output) but average selling prices were cut amid industry supply-demand adjustment, tougher domestic competition and its own active market-penetration strategy; the loss also reflected higher income tax and late-payment charges from a historical tax matter, foreign-exchange losses, asset impairments, one-off costs of the H-share listing and higher R&D on large-diameter products.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 revenue RMB 1,464,882,451.01 (-17.15%); net profit attributable RMB -208,319,118.23

quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 main business (annual report): silicon carbide semiconductor materials revenue RMB 1,224,980,369.34 (-16.88%), cost RMB 1,015,536,786.27 (+2.73%), gross margin 17.10%, down 15.82 percentage points. Overseas revenue RMB 677,016,075.84 (-19.45%) at a 35.97% gross margin; domestic revenue RMB 547,964,293.50 (-13.46%) at a -6.22% gross margin (down 27.01 points). The company attributed the revenue decline to lower selling prices as domestic competition intensified, although substrate sales volume rose. All sales are direct.
quarterly_data.figure: SiC materials revenue RMB 1,224,980,369.34 (-16.88%), gross margin 17.10%; overseas gross margin 35.97%, domestic -6.22%

quarterly_data.signal: Output and capacity (annual report): 2025 SiC substrate output 69.04 ten-thousand pieces (+68.31%), sales volume 63.33 ten-thousand pieces (+75.33%), inventory 16.11 ten-thousand pieces (+54.90%); output was 41.02 ten-thousand pieces in 2024. The Shandong (Jinan) and Shanghai (Lingang) bases have a combined designed annual capacity of more than 50 ten-thousand SiC substrates; both plants are advancing second-phase capacity plans and an overseas plant is gradually entering the planned-construction stage. The Shanghai base reached 30 ten-thousand pieces a year of capacity in H1 2024, against an original 2026 target.
quarterly_data.figure: output 69.04 ten-thousand pieces (+68.31%); sales 63.33 ten-thousand pieces (+75.33%); designed capacity over 50 ten-thousand pieces a year

quarterly_data.signal: Large-diameter transition (annual report): 8-inch products were about 44% of main-business revenue in 2025, up from 30% in 2024. The company cites a Fuji Keizai report (March 2026) putting its 2025 share of the global conductive SiC substrate market at 27.6% (first), with 27.5% of the 6-inch and 51.3% of the 8-inch market. It launched the industry's first 12-inch SiC substrate in November 2024, completed the full 12-inch range (conductive N-type, conductive P-type and semi-insulating) in Q1 2025, and says 12-inch substrates have won orders from leading customers and been delivered.
quarterly_data.figure: 8-inch about 44% of main-business revenue (30% in 2024); 12-inch orders won and delivered; 51.3% of 8-inch market (Fuji Keizai)

quarterly_data.signal: New applications (annual report): the company said semi-insulating SiC substrates are now used as the heat-dissipation layer of high-power laser chips, in batch shipments; for AI data-center power it is working closely with leading global power-device makers on next-generation power-management chips; and in advanced packaging it is working with leading global customers on SiC applications, including advanced-packaging heat-dissipation interposers. It says its substrates serve AI data-center high-efficiency power supplies, PSU, HVDC and SST, and that it has business relationships with more than half of the world's top ten power-semiconductor device makers.

Partner Shunyu Aolai Micro-Nano Optics (Shanghai) (annual report): in July 2025 SICC reached a strategic cooperation with it to combine SiC materials with its optical technology and push SiC substrates into optical applications such as AI-glasses waveguides; SICC says it has joint-development relationships with leading global optics companies.

Customer Bosch (annual report): SICC says its long-term strategic partnership with Bosch deepened, citing the Bosch Global Supplier Award it received in October 2025 as a sign of deeper supply-chain ties.

Top five customers (annual report) were 57.14% of 2025 sales (RMB 83,702.77 ten-thousand); individual shares 20.17% (RMB 29,548.35 ten-thousand), 12.65%, 9.54%, 8.40% and 6.37%; names not disclosed; related-party share of sales 0%.

Top five suppliers (annual report) were 42.99% of 2025 purchases (RMB 65,479.88 ten-thousand); individual shares 17.07% (RMB 25,997.75 ten-thousand), 7.70%, 7.08%, 6.25% and 4.89%; names not disclosed; related-party share 0%. Purchases include carbon powder, silicon powder, graphite insulation and crystal-growth, slicing, grinding and polishing equipment; the company signs long-term agreements for key materials such as graphite insulation.

R&D (annual report): 2025 R&D expense RMB 165,836,009.30, up 16.91%, 11.32% of revenue (8.02% in 2024), all expensed; spending went mainly to 12-inch substrates, 8-inch industrialisation, P-type substrates and optical / advanced-packaging applications. R&D staff 179 (13.74% of employees). Main projects include liquid-phase growth of high-quality P-type SiC substrates (budget RMB 60,550,000.00, sample stage), SiC crystal laser lift-off (budget RMB 31,885,000.00, pilot stage) and large-diameter diamond substrates (budget RMB 16,865,700.00, research stage). Cumulative grants: 203 invention patents and 308 utility-model patents.

Construction in progress (annual report): RMB 128,805,758.76 at end-2025 (+36.92%), for the Shanghai SiC project phase II (budget RMB 134,000,000.00; 26.46% of budget invested, 32.89% complete); construction in progress also includes a Malaysia project (RMB 694,133.90). The company says it is laying out overseas capacity in Southeast Asia and elsewhere. The IPO-funded SiC semiconductor materials project (RMB 200,000.00 ten-thousand planned) reached usable state in 2023.
quarterly_data.figure: construction in progress RMB 128,805,758.76 (+36.92%); Shanghai phase II 32.89% complete

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 business plan (annual report, company guidance): optimise 6/8-inch line capacity at Jinan and Shanghai Lingang and pursue capital spending prudently to lift effective utilisation; keep raising the 8-inch share in 2026 and speed volume adoption by more automotive and industrial customers; advance 12-inch work with leading customers ahead of scale delivery; price on value and avoid 'involution' price competition to protect healthy industry margins; raise the non-automotive share of revenue through AI data-center power, advanced-packaging heat dissipation and AI/AR-glasses waveguides; set staged targets for unit cost; build overseas sales and support ahead of overseas capacity; and keep R&D intensity on 12-inch, liquid-phase P-type, optical, advanced-packaging thermal and RF materials. The company says profitability is expected to recover as cost-down gains and penetration rise.
